name: Celeste Park
significance: Celeste's private note-to-self that her recoverable calendar entry is only half the documentary picture of the off-calendar meeting.
infoNote: Signals that Nina Sen holds or can access the matching authorization record, which paired with Celeste's calendar entry establishes that Vale was given limited Parallax access.

name: Graham Pike
significance: Graham privately enjoys his critics' line that he is an arsonist who buys insurance first, and adopted it as his own motto.

name: Sam Vale
significance: Sam's shorthand for the ordinary, unmythologized Vale she knew: the person who forgot the groceries.

name: Morgan Shaw
significance: Morgan's working label for the loose end in the client's surveillance photographs of the camera-fitted vehicle.
infoNote: Flags that the plate in the client's photos resolves to a fleet-leasing company dissolved last year, a shell Celeste or Rosa could try to trace before anyone treats the pictures as proof of surveillance.

name: Kit Rakes
significance: Kit's battered theory notebook and the six theories it holds are the center of Kit's professional identity.

name: Rosa Baptiste
significance: The half-memory Rosa cannot quite fix: a cyclist clipped by a delivery robot at the service crossing about a week and a half before the party.
infoNote: Points at the delivery-robot incident at the service crossing, which connects Rosa's fuzzy recollection to a courier's claims notice and gives Manny, Dee, or Morgan a concrete thing to ask about.

name: Ash Salerno
significance: What Ash lost in the scandal was not eyesight but the benefit of the doubt, the phrase Ash repeats to explain the last several years.

name: Dr. Farah Haddad
significance: Farah's professional creed that provenance is not purity: a record can be old and deceptive, or authentic and misleading.

name: Dorian Ashe
significance: Dorian's guiding belief, and self-justification, that narrative is itself a form of truth.

name: Manny Diallo
significance: Manny's rule of the trade: the apps see everything and understand almost nothing.
